chunks: Ja'far ibn Ali narrated to me from his father, from al-Husayn, from his father al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abdillah ibn al-Mughira, from al-Abbas ibn Amir, from Abi al-Sahari, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the drinker of wine (khamr), and he said: Allah does not accept his prayer as long as there is any trace of it in his veins.
ai.seo_question: How long is a wine drinker's prayer not accepted according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) ruled that the prayer of a wine drinker is not accepted by Allah as long as any trace of the wine remains in their body, a ruling derived from the literal interpretation of 'urūq' (veins). This establishes a specific condition for the validity of salat related to ritual impurity or state of intoxication, distinguishing it from general impurity (najāsah) by linking spiritual acceptance to the physical persistence of the substance. In Shia jurisprudence, this highlights the profound connection between physical purity and spiritual receptivity, emphasizing that intoxication creates a barrier to divine acceptance that persists until the substance is fully metabolized or expelled.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 7. It was narrated to me by Ja’far b. Ali from his father from al-Hussain from his father al-Hassan b. Ali from Abdillah b. al-Mughira from al-Abbas b. ’Amir from Abi al-Sahari from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said:
Once Imam Ja’far Sadiq was asked about the ruling regarding a drunkard. Imam (a.s.) replied, “His prayers will not be accepted till a time even a single drop of wine is present in his veins.”
